question: A 4-year-old boy presents to his pediatrician for severe developmental delay. On exam he is noted to have macroorchidism, hypertelorism, large protruding ears, a large jaw, and a long thin face. Suspicious of what the diagnosis may be, the pediatrician orders a PCR and DNA sequencing. The results reveal an expansion of 250 repeats of CGG. What is the diagnosis of the boy?

nodes: Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorder, Complementation Group G
paths: (Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorder, Complementation Group G)-CAUSES->(Neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease)-CAUSES->(Disease)-CAUSES->(Fragile X Syndrome)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Expansion of 250 repeats of CGG" -> "Fragile X syndrome" -> 95% CHAIN: "Macroorchidism, hypertelorism, large protruding ears, large jaw, long thin face" -> "Suspicion of Fragile X syndrome" -> 90% CHAIN: "PCR and DNA sequencing" -> "Confirmation of Fragile X syndrome" -> 95%
enhanced_information: The 4-year-old boy with macroorchidism, hypertelorism, large protruding ears, a large jaw, and a long thin face, along with an expansion of 250 repeats of CGG on PCR and DNA sequencing, is most likely diagnosed with Fragile X syndrome. The presence of these physical features and the genetic finding strongly support this diagnosis.
analysis: The clinical presentation of macroorchidism, hypertelorism, large protruding ears, a large jaw, and a long thin face, along with an expansion of 250 repeats of CGG on PCR and DNA sequencing, is highly indicative of Fragile X syndrome. Fragile X syndrome is associated with a CGG repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene, leading to the characteristic physical features and developmental delay seen in this patient. The other options do not align with the specific findings in this case.
